Class FillRecorder

java.lang.Object
com.leap.leaplaughlove.order.history.FillRecorder
@Component public class FillRecorder extends Object
Writes everything a fill leaves behind: the FILLED execution, the cash settlement and holding update (delegated to account-app via AccountClient), and its position movement in the audit ledger. Shared by live order submission and SeededFillService, so a seeded fill is booked exactly the way a real one is.

A fill is booked in three steps, and callers must commit between them:

  1. recordExecution(Order, BigDecimal, OffsetDateTime) inside a transaction, which must commit before settling: account-app writes the settlement on its own database connection, and its ledger rows reference the order and the execution by foreign key, so it can't see either while this app's transaction is still open.
  2. settle(Order, Execution, String) outside any transaction.
  3. recordPositionMovement(Order, Execution) inside a transaction, only once settling succeeded: account-app builds portfolio history from position movements, so one must never exist for a fill that didn't settle.

    • recordExecution

      public Execution recordExecution(Order order, BigDecimal price, OffsetDateTime time)
      Writes the FILLED execution for a fill of the whole order at one price. Does not change the order's own status.
      Parameters:
      order - the order being filled
      price - the execution price per share
      time - when the fill happened; stamped on every row the fill writes
      Returns:
      the saved FILLED execution

    • settle

      public SettlementResponse settle(Order order, Execution execution, String bearerToken)
      Settles a committed execution with account-app: posts the cash and updates the holding. Safe to repeat - account-app settles each execution once and answers a repeat from the state it already booked.
      Parameters:
      order - the filled order
      execution - its committed FILLED execution
      bearerToken - the token to call account-app with, or null to forward the current request's own
      Returns:
      account-app's settlement result

    • isRefused

      public static boolean isRefused(RuntimeException failure)
      Tells whether a failed settle(Order, Execution, String) means account-app refused the fill, so nothing was booked. account-app settles in one transaction and answers a refusal (e.g. not enough shares to sell) with a 4xx. Anything else - no answer (unreachable, timed out), a 5xx, or a failure on this side - leaves it unknown whether cash and holdings moved. Such a fill must not be recorded as rejected: it is left for PendingFillRecovery to settle again, which is safe because account-app settles each execution only once.
      Parameters:
      failure - what settle(Order, Execution, String) threw
      Returns:
      true only if account-app answered with a refusal

    • refusalReason

      public static String refusalReason(RuntimeException refusal)
      account-app's own explanation of a refused settlement, e.g. "Cannot settle sell: insufficient position quantity", read from the message of its error body.
      Parameters:
      refusal - what settle(Order, Execution, String) threw, for which isRefused(RuntimeException) is true
      Returns:
      the reason, or the exception's message if the body has none

    • completeFill

      public boolean completeFill(Order lockedOrder, Execution execution)
      Finishes booking a settled live fill: writes its position movement and marks the order FILLED. Call inside a transaction holding the order's row lock (see OrderRepository#findByIdForUpdate), so live submission and PendingFillRecovery can't both finish it. Does nothing if the fill was already finished.
      Parameters:
      lockedOrder - the order, loaded with its row lock in the current transaction
      execution - its settled FILLED execution
      Returns:
      true if this call finished the fill, false if it was already finished
